heroHeadline: 'Project Freedom' Begins: US Navy Escorts Hormuz Ships; Iran Threatens Attack on US Forces; Ceasefire at Maximum Strain
heroSubtitle: Trump launched 'Project Freedom' on May 3 (Day 65) — deploying guided-missile destroyers, 100+ aircraft, and ~15,000 service members to escort ~2,000 stranded commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran immediately threatened: 'Any foreign armed forces, especially the aggressive US army, will be attacked.' Brent crude surged above $103–106/bbl and US gas prices hit $4.44/gallon nationally. Simultaneously, Iran submitted a 14-point counter-proposal to end the war (May 2); Trump called himself 'dissatisfied' and said his options were 'striking a deal or to blast the hell out of them and finish them forever.' Trump also formally notified Congress on May 3 that the Iran ceasefire reset the War Powers Resolution 60-day clock — a legal theory Democrats rejected, continuing to explore litigation. A Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos poll (May 3) recorded 62% disapproval — a second-term record high — with multiple simultaneous polls converging at 33–37% approval driven by the Iran war, cost of living, and declining trust in Trump's promises. Kevin Warsh's Senate floor vote is set for the week of May 11, before Powell exits May 15. The $70B ICE/CBP reconciliation Senate vote is also targeting May 11.
